claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

hospital_abroad.description: Whether the child is in hospital abroad.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you some questions.

Let's start with the basics:

**Do you have any children you're responsible for, and if so, how many?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I have a child - my son Alex. He's three years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. So you have one child, Alex, who is 3 years old.

Now I need to ask you a few more questions to assess your eligibility:

**Do you currently live in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great, thank you. Now I need to understand your responsibility for Alex:

**Does Alex live with you?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he doesn't live with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. Since Alex doesn't live with you, I need to understand your situation better.

**Are you paying at least the same amount as Child Benefit (or the equivalent in kind) towards looking after Alex - for example on food, clothes or pocket money?**

(For reference, Child Benefit is currently £25.60 per week for the eldest/only child, so around £111 per month)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I do contribute towards his upkeep. I help with things like clothes, toys, and other things he needs. I give about £50 a week.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing that information. That's helpful to know.

Now I have a few more questions:

**Who does Alex currently live with?** (For example, does he live with his other parent, a relative, or someone else?)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He lives with his mum, my ex-partner.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that. Now I need to ask:

**Is Alex's mum currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, she isn't claiming Child Benefit for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. I have a few more questions to complete the assessment:

**Do you have the right to reside in the UK?** (For example, are you a British citizen, do you have settled status, or do you have another immigration status?)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I'm a British citizen.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect, thank you. Just a couple more questions to complete my assessment:

**Is Alex in any of the following situations:**
- In hospital or residential care for an extended period?
- In local authority care?
- Working 24 hours or more per week?
- Claiming benefits in his own right?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, actually Alex is in hospital. He's been in hospital abroad for treatment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I'm sorry to hear Alex is in hospital. I need to understand this situation better as it may affect eligibility:

**How long has Alex been in hospital abroad?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He's been there for a couple of months now.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. I need to ask a few more questions about Alex's hospital stay:

**Did Alex go abroad specifically to be in hospital for treatment, or was he already living abroad when he went into hospital?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'm not entirely sure about all the specifics of that situation.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That's okay. Let me ask a related question to help clarify:

**Are you still in the UK, and do you continue to regularly spend money on Alex while he's in hospital abroad?** (You've mentioned you contribute £50 a week - has this continued during his hospital stay?)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'm not really sure about all those details to be honest.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I understand - these are complex circumstances. Let me ask one more important question:

**Just to clarify - is Alex's mum (who he normally lives with) in the UK, or is she abroad with Alex while he's in hospital?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'm not certain about those arrangements, I'm afraid.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for being honest about what you know and don't know. Let me ask one final question to help complete my assessment:

**When Alex is not in hospital, does he normally live in the UK with his mum, or does he normally live abroad?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: When he's not in hospital, he normally lives here in the UK with his mum.

## Summary of Your Child Benefit Eligibility Assessment

Based on the information you've provided, I'm unable to make a definitive determination about your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex. Here's why:

### What works in your favor:
- You are a British citizen living in the UK
- Alex is only 3 years old (well under the age limit)
- You contribute £50 per week towards Alex's upkeep, which is more than the Child Benefit rate
- Alex's mum is not currently claiming Child Benefit for him
- Under normal circumstances, you could qualify even though Alex doesn't live with you, because you're making sufficient financial contributions

### The complicating factor:
Alex has been in hospital abroad for approximately two months. The rules around children in hospital are complex:
- There's a 12-week time limit for children in hospital before Child Benefit may be affected
- For children in hospital abroad, you may still qualify if Alex only went abroad for hospital treatment AND you're regularly spending money on him
- However, you don't have enough information about the specific circumstances to determine if these exceptions apply

### What you could do next:
I'd recommend contacting the Child Benefit Office directly. They can:
- Help you understand whether Alex's hospital stay abroad affects your eligibility
- Guide you through making a claim if you're eligible
- Answer specific questions about your circumstances

You may also want to check with Alex's mum about the details of the hospital arrangements, as this information would be important for any claim.

These are critical factors that would determine whether an exception to the hospital rules applies and whether Child Benefit eligibility continues beyond the 12-week threshold.

Given the lack of clarity on these essential details and the complexity of the rules around children in hospital abroad, eligibility cannot be definitively determined.
